title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: Own the compounder, trail your stop upward, and demand 1.5x+ asymmetry before adding the next rupee.
epigraph.author: Institutional Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: Our refreshed Pass 1 and Pass 2 review weighs both sides without bias. In Pass 1, MCX kept COMPOUNDER_PASS with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. Q2 FY27 F&O ADT hit ₹12.63 lakh crore, H1 clients reached 19.8 lakh, and Core SGF grew to ₹1,472.16 crore [29, 30]. GIFT City IIBX's volume collapse also confirmed MCX's domestic moat [34]. Yet Pass 1 weakened our static-IT-cost view and flagged recurring capacity IT opex [28, 29]. It also surfaced ~10% CME energy royalties, ~25% normalized tax, temporary SGF relief, 15% dividend payout, and SEBI's May 2025 ₹25 lakh fine [28, 29, 31, 32, 33]. In Pass 2, those frictions trim our Base Target to ₹4,150. We keep our 25 shares on HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP and hold new cash at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT.

Active regulatory and operational governance watchpoints justify PASS_WITH_WATCH and a disciplined 44x (not 55x+) exit multiple.

1. Short-Term (1–3 Months): Hold starter shares; wait to add. RSI cooled to 55.82 (CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION). Still, 7 distribution days and 1.06:1 CMP R:R favor waiting for ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00.

3. Long-Term (3–5+ Years): COMPOUNDER_PASS (PASS_WITH_WATCH). Over 98%–99% market share, zero debt, and 71.4% ROCE anchor a core franchise. Watch SEBI rules, IT opex, and payout discipline.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of truth for our refreshed MCX monograph. Every Pass 1 assumption audit, blind-spot patch, Reverse DCF table, and multi-timeframe moving-average check leads to a clear, disciplined action plan.

Both sides of the aisle are grounded in verified facts. The bull case remains extraordinary: MCX controls more than 98% to 99% of India's non-agricultural commodity derivatives market, holds ₹1,472.16 crore in Core SGF with zero debt and 71.4% ROCE, and just posted 76% operating margins on ₹800 crore of Q2 FY27 revenue as 19.8 lakh H1 clients traded gold, silver, crude, natural gas, and electricity contracts—while GIFT City's IIBX gold volume collapsed to 916.2 kg.

The bear case is sharper after our Pass 1 refresh. Management confirmed that higher IT spending is recurring operational opex to double exchange capacity, CME energy royalties scale with crude turnover, normalized effective tax rates are stepping up from 21.2% toward ~25%, and Q2's zero SGF contribution is only temporary. Add compressed 15% dividend payout (0.22% yield), SEBI's May 2025 ₹25 lakh disclosure penalty, and silver hitting a 14-month low on November 25, and you see why we trimmed our Base Case target from ₹4,300 to ₹4,150.

Weighting our refreshed scenarios—25% Bull at ₹5,000, 50% Base at ₹4,150, and 25% Bear at ₹2,350—produces a probability-weighted expected value of ₹3,912.50 (+9.2% vs. ledger CMP ₹3,581.60; +13.1% vs. our ₹3,460.00 support top). At ₹3,581.60, reward-to-risk to ₹4,150 against our ratcheted ₹3,043.24 stop is only 1.06-to-1. On a modest 3.4% pullback to ₹3,460.00, it expands to 1.66-to-1.

That split gives us a crystal-clear two-part posture. Because our Zerodha account now holds 25 shares of MCX at ₹3,494.40 average cost (+2.50% gain, 2.10% portfolio weight), our holding action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP—keep your starter shares working, ratchet your protective GTT stop UP from ₹3,033.74 to ₹3,043.24, and clean out the expired OPT-IN-002 ledger item.

For fresh capital, our verdict remains WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. We keep 100% of our next marginal cash unit in liquid cash—benchmarking against shortlist name ZYDUSLIFE (0%) and depository peer CDSL (0%)—and wait to add a second MCX tranche only inside ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00.

Pause for a moment on portfolio risk arithmetic, because position sizing is where good research turns into durable compounding. Across our ₹42.60 lakh Indian equity net worth—with ₹15.39 lakh sitting in cash—our 25 MCX shares represent ₹89,540 of market value, or 2.10% weight. From the ₹3,581.60 ledger close down to our ratcheted ₹3,043.24 hard stop, total dollar risk on the existing position is approximately ₹13,459, or just 0.32% of portfolio equity. Even if we later add a matching second tranche near ₹3,460.00 on a calm pullback, combined position risk stays near 0.60% of net worth—leaving plenty of cushion for MCX's ₹128.45 daily Average True Range without ever letting a single commodity-volatility swing rattle the wider book.

Our 100%-reconciled capital redeployment comparison underscores why keeping that next marginal rupee in cash is an active choice, not indecision. Shortlist candidate ZYDUSLIFE (₹1,236.00 on the November 25 TradingView feed, 2.03:1 support R:R) is already a 3.24% Zerodha holding across 115 shares, while outside depository peer CDSL (₹1,413.00 on November 25 TV, 2.24:1 support R:R) trades at 58.5x earnings for 32.0% ROCE—nearly eight turns richer than MCX for less than half the return on capital. Holding our 25 MCX shares with a ratcheted ₹3,043.24 stop and letting cash wait for ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00 keeps capital aligned with both quality and asymmetry.

book_subsections.title: Five Quarterly Signposts & Clear Upgrade/Downgrade Rules
paragraphs: Every open position needs pre-committed rules so emotion never takes the wheel. To upgrade fresh capital from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to an active add, we want either a calm-volume pullback into ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00 (delivering 1.66-to-1 asymmetry) or Q3 FY27 options premium ADT breaking cleanly above ₹12,000 crore while recurring IT opex stays contained.

To downgrade MCX to an immediate exit, watch three hard tripwires: a daily or weekly close below our ratcheted ₹3,043.24 stop-loss (breaking the 30-week SMA); a repeat multi-hour exchange outage following the October 2025 incident; or a SEBI circular cutting commodity options fees or curbing weekly expiries.

Between now and the next earnings release, monitor five operational signposts: options premium ADT (vs. Q2's ₹10,291 crore), recurring IT opex as processing capacity doubles, effective tax rate convergence around ~25% alongside SGF contribution resumption, FY27 dividend payout recovery above FY26's 15% trough, and SEBI updates on data-centre relocation and FPI bullion access.

With 25 shares already on the books at ₹3,494.40 and risking just 0.32% of total portfolio equity down to ₹3,043.24, we have the best of both worlds: upside participation if MCX runs straight to ₹4,150+, and dry powder ready at ₹3,460 if commodity volatility hands us a better pitch.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Hold the Starter, Stay Patient on the Add
book_callouts.text: When you already own a 2.10% starter position in a 71%-ROCE monopoly at ₹3,494.40, you never need to chase at 1.06:1 R:R. Ratchet your stop upward to ₹3,043.24, let the starter compound, and make the market pay you 1.66:1 at ₹3,460 before adding.
